introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 3 (0760), Paper 3 - Africa and World History, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing ONE from each of the four sections (Section A: Africa, 1800-1945; Section B: Africa, 1945 to the present; Section C: World Revolutions and Diplomacy, 1700-1919; Section D: World, 1919 to the present date). All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown: **SECTION D: WORLD, 1919 TO THE PRESENT DATE**
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « answer FOUR questions, choosing ONE from each of the four sections ». `regles_choix` porte une règle « 1 sur 3 » par section (A, B, C, D), ce qui correspond exactement à la consigne imprimée ; la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : chaque question porte 25 marks imprimés (« All questions carry equal marks »), soit 100 points pour les quatre questions à traiter. Aucun écart de points constaté ; `points` vaut 25 pour l'exercice et pour l'unique question de chaque fichier.

Sujet scanné de deux pages (page de garde et questions 1 à 12) ; filigranes gcerevision ignorés. Le texte de la page 2 transparaît en miroir sur la page de garde (verso mal opacifié) et quelques espaces sont manquants à l'impression (question 8 : « between1871and1890 », rétabli en « between 1871 and 1890 ») ; aucune question coupée ni illisible, aucune figure ni carte dans le sujet.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level (introduction, développement, conclusion argumentée). Aucune citation n'est inventée et les chiffres sont limités à des repères datés de l'historiographie courante (dates, traités) ; à relire par un historien avant mise en vente.

Question 4 : l'énoncé imprimé date le déclenchement de la révolte Mau Mau de 1951. L'historiographie situe la montée de la violence en 1950-52 (mouvement interdit en août 1950, état d'urgence proclamé le 20 octobre 1952) ; le sujet est recopié tel quel et le corrigé précise la chronologie sans corriger l'énoncé.

Question 5 : l'Afrique équatoriale française regroupe le Gabon, le Moyen-Congo, l'Oubangui-Chari et le Tchad ; le Cameroun, ancien mandat puis tutelle, n'en faisait pas partie. Les interventions militaires françaises (Gabon 1964, Tchad à partir de la fin des années 1960, Centrafrique 1979) et le rôle du réseau Foccart sont cités selon l'historiographie courante, sans chiffres.

Question 7 : le sujet emploie « romanisation » au sens de la promotion du catholicisme romain par Jacques II ; les dates de 1688 sont données en style ancien (naissance du prince le 10 juin, acquittement des sept évêques et invitation à Guillaume le 30 juin, débarquement à Torbay le 5 novembre).

Question 9 : le montant des réparations (132 milliards de marks-or, fixé en 1921) et les pertes territoriales sont cités de mémoire historique établie ; aucune statistique de population n'est avancée.

Question 11 : la Banque mondiale et le FMI sont des institutions spécialisées de l'ONU ; l'UNICEF (fonds et non institution spécialisée) n'est volontairement pas traité. Les dates (variole déclarée éradiquée en 1980, Alma-Ata 1978, convention 182 de l'OIT en 1999, Codex Alimentarius 1963, retrait des États-Unis de l'UNESCO en 1984-85) sont citées selon l'historiographie courante.

Question 12 : le sujet vise la rupture sino-soviétique après la mort de Staline (1953). Les dates (discours de Khrouchtchev en février 1956, rupture de l'accord nucléaire en 1959, retrait des conseillers en 1960, congrès de Bucarest en juin 1960, guerre sino-indienne 1962, incidents de l'Oussouri en mars 1969) sont données selon l'historiographie courante ; aucun chiffre n'est avancé.

Thèmes : les noms sont qualifiés pour éviter les collisions avec les Tags de l'Histoire francophone (`sino-soviet split`, `afrikaner nationalism`, `mau mau revolt in kenya`...) ; plusieurs sont réutilisés des sujets History 2020-2021 (`scramble for africa`, `apartheid in south africa`, `cold war`, `indirect rule in colonial africa`) ; à revérifier à l'ingestion avec `find_tag_variant`.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Critically examine the contributions of UN Specialized Agencies in enhancing social and economic progress in the world.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The United Nations Specialized Agencies are autonomous international organisations linked to the UN by agreements through the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC). They include the International Labour Organization (ILO, founded in 1919 and made a UN agency in 1946), the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO, 1945), the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO, 1945), the World Health Organization (WHO, 1948), and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, created at the Bretton Woods Conference of 1944. Others deal with specific technical fields, such as the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). This essay examines their contributions to social and economic progress, and criticisms of their work.

**1. Contributions.**
- *Health (WHO).* WHO coordinated the worldwide campaign against smallpox, which was declared eradicated in 1980, the first human disease to be eliminated. It has led immunisation campaigns against polio (cases fell very sharply and the disease is now confined to a very few countries), supported programmes against malaria, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS, set international health standards, and promoted primary health care in the Alma-Ata Declaration (1978). The Onchocerciasis Control Programme in West Africa, started in 1974 with the World Bank, UNDP and FAO, reduced river blindness.
- *Food and agriculture (FAO and IFAD).* FAO gives technical advice on crops, fisheries and forests, collects data, gives early warning of food shortages, and helped to introduce improved varieties and methods; with WHO it created the Codex Alimentarius (1963) to set food safety standards. IFAD finances rural development projects for poor small farmers.
- *Education and culture (UNESCO).* UNESCO campaigned for literacy and universal primary education, supported teacher training, and promoted the protection of cultural and natural heritage through the World Heritage Convention (1972).
- *Labour (ILO).* The ILO adopted international labour standards on working conditions, freedom of association, child labour (for example Convention 182 of 1999 on the worst forms) and forced labour, which many states incorporated into their laws.
- *Finance and development (IMF and World Bank).* The World Bank financed roads, dams, schools and hospitals, notably through the International Development Association (1960) which gives low-interest loans to the poorest countries, and the IMF helped countries with balance-of-payments difficulties and supported monetary stability.
- *Technical cooperation.* The ITU, WMO, Universal Postal Union and ICAO made possible international communication, weather forecasting and safe air travel, which support trade and development.

**2. Criticisms and limitations.**
- *Financial and political dependence.* The agencies rely on contributions from member states, mainly rich ones, and the withdrawal or reduction of funding (for example the departure of the USA and the United Kingdom from UNESCO in 1984-85) affected their work. Their actions depend on the consent of governments, so they cannot force a state to act.
- *Structural adjustment.* In the 1980s and 1990s IMF and World Bank programmes in Africa and elsewhere required cuts in public spending, privatisation and currency devaluation, which many critics said reduced spending on health and education and increased poverty. Voting power in both institutions is weighted by financial contributions, so rich countries dominate.
- *Uneven results.* Many problems remain: famine, malnutrition, illiteracy and preventable disease persist in many poor countries, and the response to some crises (for example the early phase of the 2014 Ebola outbreak in West Africa) was criticised as slow.
- *Bureaucracy, duplication and politicisation.* Overlap between agencies, administrative costs and the influence of Cold War and later political rivalries reduced efficiency.
- *Limited resources compared with the scale of problems.* The needs of developing countries were much greater than the funds available.

**3. Evaluation.** The agencies' contributions were substantial and often decisive in specific fields, especially health (smallpox, polio), food and agricultural technology, standards for labour and communication, and the financing of development. Their weakness lies in their dependence on powerful states and in some policies, such as strict conditions attached to loans, which sometimes harmed the social progress they were supposed to help. They are therefore most effective when they act as technical and coordinating bodies with the cooperation of national governments.

**Conclusion.** The UN Specialized Agencies made major contributions to social and economic progress in the world, but their record is uneven and limited by funding, politics and sometimes the nature of their policies.
